subject: Processing scope mapping and retention escape clauses
body:
From: Alice Patel <alice.patel@medicore.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: privacy@medicore.com
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Processing scope + retention carveouts (initial questionnaire)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Attached is our standard onboarding privacy questionnaire and a short list of follow-ups we need to close before Legal approves the DPA. High level asks:

- A clear mapping of which Redwood components process PII vs non-PII for inference requests (we need a table per service).
- Dataflow diagram (ingest -> storage -> inference -> logs) with zones labeled (control plane, customer KV, ephemeral token stores).
- Retention carveouts: we have a few required exceptions for audit/anti-abuse logs — please surface any DPA language that would prevent those.
- Subprocessor list (for dedicated/private we need onshore/offshore distinctions).

I've attached the questionnaire (Medicore_Privacy_Questionnaire.xlsx). Can you share a short walkthrough next week? If possible, include any redline candidates for Section 4 (Data Retention) and Section 6 (Subprocessors).

Appreciate it —
Alice
Alice Patel
Head of Privacy, Medicore Health
alice.patel@medicore.com
(415) 555-0119

---
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Patel <alice.patel@medicore.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-01T13:40:12Z
Subject: Re: Processing scope + retention carveouts (initial questionnaire)

Alice —

Thanks for the questionnaire and the clear asks. I had our privacy/tech leads start a short mapping; attached is a 1‑page summary (processing-scope-summary.pdf) that highlights which subsystems touch inferred text, telemetry, and customer-supplied PII.

Quick notes from our side:
- Inference requests: model input and output are considered customer content. Persistent storage of that content only occurs if a customer enables long-term logging; default hosted retention is 30 days for telemetry and 90 days for indexed audit logs.
- Ephemeral caches (KV cache/KV cache shards) are cleared per-session by default; we can provide an architectural note if Medicore needs deterministic zeroing.
- Control plane telemetry (scheduler, autoscaler events) contains only ephemeral IDs; user-identifying fields are redacted unless explicitly ingested by the customer during setup.

For the DPA redlines: we can propose language that allows retention exceptions for fraud/abuse investigation with a documented legal request and a 30‑day retention limit, unless otherwise required by law. We will mark that as a possible carveout and circulate a proposed clause.

Would next Wednesday at 10:00 PT work for a 30‑minute walkthrough? Kimberly will cover the dataflow diagram and Marissa will handle the subprocessor/contracting questions.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: processing-scope-summary.pdf (summary of subsystem responsibilities and default retention windows)

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Patel <alice.patel@medicore.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-02T08:30:05Z
Subject: Re: Processing scope + retention carveouts (dataflow & classification)

Folks —

I've attached an updated diagram (dataflow_v2.png) and a quick CSV export of how we classify fields in incoming payloads (pii-classification.csv). Highlights:

- Ingest: requests hit our edge ingress (region-specific endpoints). We tokenize request IDs and immediately drop raw network-level metadata after 72 hours unless the customer enables enhanced troubleshooting.
- Storage: model artifacts and user telemetry are logically separated. Customer content retention is controlled per-customer via tenant config.
- Subprocessors: for hosted API we use two main subprocessors (regionally mapped):
  * GPU rendering (US/EU regional pools) — vendor: VectorGrid Ltd (onshore/nearshore options)
  * Long-term object storage — vendor: ArchiveSafe (primary: US, backup: EU)
  Full list can be provided in CSV; for Private/Dedicated customers we can provide an inventory and narrow down which vendors are used.

On retention carveouts and the DPA:
- We can support a documented exception process: legal request -> internal access approval -> limited retention window (30 days) -> automated purge.
- For audit logs required by regulation, we recommend enumerating specific log categories and a maximum retention in the annex rather than a blanket exclusion.

Action items I recommend before the walkthrough:
1) Medicore to flag any log categories that require retention >90 days (security/audit/clinical QA).
2) Medicore to indicate whether onshore-only subprocessors are required for certain data classes.
3) Redwood to provide a redline of Section 4/6 for review (Soojin).

-Kim

Attachments: dataflow_v2.png (annotated), pii-classification.csv (field-level classification)

---
From: Alice Patel <alice.patel@medicore.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, privacy@medicore.com
Date: 2026-12-03T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Processing scope + retention carveouts (next steps)

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple quick follow-ups before the call on Wednesday:

1) Can you export the subprocessor inventory that applies to the hosted API (vendor + region + function)? We need it for our procurement team to confirm onshore/offshore constraints.
2) For the retention exception flow, please confirm whether the exception can be scoped per-tenant (i.e., Medicore requests an exception only for a specific tenant ID) and whether retention triggers an automatic email to Medicore legal when an exception is created/extended.
3) Please include a proposed redline for the DPA Section 4 that limits exceptions to documented legal requests with an explicit 30-day cap and audit trail.

If you can drop those items in the Drive link you shared, we can circulate internally to Legal and procurement ahead of the walkthrough.

Best regards,
Alice

---
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Patel <alice.patel@medicore.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-03T14:02:10Z
Subject: Re: Processing scope + retention carveouts (confirmation)

Alice —

We will:
- Produce the hosted-API subprocessor CSV by EOD today and drop it in the shared Drive folder (includes vendor function, primary region, and data handling notes).
- Confirm per-tenant scoping for exceptions is supported; exceptions will be scoped to tenant IDs and will generate an audit event (and notification to a configured legal contact).
- Circulate a DPA redline (Section 4/6) that reads as an exception process: documented legal request + internal approval + 30-day retention cap + audit trail.

Marissa will share the procurement-friendly subprocessor export. Kimberly will attach a short note describing where logs live and the purge automation.

Call is set for 2026-12-09 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent).

Thanks —
Soojin
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

(attachment list repeated above)
